ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The table title is “Virtual water content of some agricultural products in Israel in 1999,” listing the amount of virtual water needed to produce each kilogram of different agricultural products. In the table, dairy cattle are about 177.8 m³/kg, laying hens about 31.09 m³/kg, and beef cattle about 15.5 m³/kg, with relatively high virtual water content; barley about 5.87, wheat about 4.067, and poultry about 5.434 are in the middle; carrots about 0.064, vegetables about 0.069, bananas about 0.252, and citrus about 0.64 are relatively low. Reasoning: The arid regions of Northwest China have a shortage of water resources. From the perspective of virtual water, it is not suitable to maintain or expand large-scale production of high-water-consumption, high-virtual-water agricultural products, but should reduce the proportion of high-virtual-water agricultural products and increase the proportion of low-virtual-water or water-saving agricultural products. This practice of changing the internal proportions of planting, breeding, and products in agriculture is summarized as adjusting the agricultural structure.
